title: Elevated ICP / cerebral herniation
keyNumbers: Hypertonic saline: 2%–23.4% as bolus, alone or with mannitol; 3% may run peripherally, ≥7.5% (incl. 23.4%) via central line
Mannitol 20%: 0.5–1 g/kg IV bolus over 5–15 min via peripheral line; may repeat q4–6h (ENLS)
NCS 2020: upper limits Na 155–160 and Cl 110–115 mEq/L may be reasonable
Intracranial hypertension: sustained (>5 min) ICP >22 mmHg (ENLS v6.0)
presentation: Declining consciousness, new unilateral fixed/dilated pupil, posturing, Cushing response (hypertension, bradycardia, irregular respirations)
Headache, vomiting, papilledema with subacute rise
definitions: Intracranial hypertension: sustained (>5 min) ICP >22 mmHg (ENLS v6.0)

immediateActions.action: HOB 30° (≤45°), head midline, loosen collar; treat fever, hypoxia, hypercarbia, pain, agitation; avoid hypotonic fluids and hyponatremia
Hyperosmolar bolus (HTS or mannitol — whichever is fastest) + brief hyperventilation as a bridge
Stat non-contrast CT head; neurosurgery for EVD (CSF diversion) or decompression
Repeat osmotherapy for symptoms/ICP; sodium and renal function q4–6h; serum osmolality/osmolar gap with mannitol
Intubate, sedate (propofol bolus/infusion), consider neuromuscular blockade, barbiturates, decompressive surgery per etiology

notes: Osmolar gap (measured − calculated osm) preferred over an osmolality threshold for mannitol AKI risk (NCS 2020)

workup.test: Na and Cl q4–6h during HTS
notes: ENLS v6.0: keep Na <160 mEq/L during HTS
NCS 2020: upper limits Na 155–160 and Cl 110–115 mEq/L may be reasonable

treatment.doseText: 2%–23.4% as bolus, alone or with mannitol; 3% may run peripherally, ≥7.5% (incl. 23.4%) via central line. No bolus volume specified by NCS 2020 or the ENLS v6.0 ICP module — use institutional protocol
notes: NCS 2020: HTS suggested over mannitol for initial ICP management in TBI and ICH; either acceptable in AIS and SAH
ENLS v6.0: mannitol and HTS have equivalent efficacy for lowering ICP
evidenceNote: NCS 2020: HTS over mannitol in TBI — conditional, low-quality evidence; in ICH — conditional, very low-quality evidence
NCS 2020: HTS or mannitol in AIS — conditional, low-quality evidence; insufficient evidence for either to improve neurological outcome

treatment.doseText: 0.5–1 g/kg IV bolus over 5–15 min via peripheral line; may repeat q4–6h (ENLS)
notes: Redose by osmolar gap; ENLS v6.0 cites gap goals of 20–55 mOsm/kg (little added benefit at high end); NCS 2020 found no evidence for a specific cutoff
Use inline filter; check for crystals
evidenceNote: NCS 2020: alternative when HTS can't be given (TBI) — conditional, low-quality evidence; either agent in AIS — conditional, low-quality evidence
NCS 2020: osmolar gap over osmolality for AKI monitoring — conditional, very low-quality evidence

treatment.doseText: Short bridge only for acute ICP elevation/herniation; mild hypocapnia (PaCO2 32–35 mmHg) if used beyond the acute bridge
notes: Cerebral vasoconstriction → ischemia risk; not a sustained therapy
evidenceNote: NCS 2020: strong recommendation, very low-quality evidence (brief episodes)
ENLS v6.0 Tier 2: PaCO2 32–35 mmHg in selected patients failing other measures; ideally with cerebral oxygen monitoring

treatment.doseText: Emergent EVD for obstructive hydrocephalus; with EVD in place, drain 5–10 mL CSF for acute ICP rise (ENLS v6.0)
Bolus 1–2 mg/kg; infusion in ventilated patients titrated to max 200 mcg/kg/min (only temporarily at that dose)
notes: Hypotension, especially with bolus — fluids/vasopressors to keep CPP
PRIS more likely >80 mcg/kg/min for >48 h

treatment.doseText: Bolus 5–15 mg/kg over 30 min–2 h, then 1–4 mg/kg/h; titrate to ICP or EEG burst suppression (5–20 s or ≥50%); continue 24–96 h
notes: High dose can mimic brain death (unreactive pupils); clearance takes days — caution prognosticating
evidenceNote: ENLS v6.0 Tier 3 (consensus; no rigorous RCTs)

treatment.doseText: Mild hypothermia 32–36 °C (TBI 35–36 °C only); hemicraniectomy as lifesaving option in selected cases

treatment.agent: Corticosteroids for edema from ICH, TBI, or stroke
treatment.doseText: Do not use (steroids remain appropriate for vasogenic edema from tumor/abscess)
evidenceNote: NCS 2020: strong recommendation against steroids in ICH (moderate-quality evidence)

treatment.agent: Prophylactic scheduled mannitol in acute ischemic stroke

pitfalls: Hyperventilation is a bridge, not a treatment — prolonged hypocapnia worsens ischemia
No proven outcome benefit from either osmotic agent — they buy time for definitive treatment
Rebound hyponatremia or abrupt HTS discontinuation can worsen edema; avoid hyponatremia in brain injury (NCS 2020)
Mannitol: an osmolality ceiling (e.g., 320) is a convention — NCS 2020 favors the osmolar gap to track accumulation
escalateWhen: Any herniation sign → neurosurgery + neuro-ICU immediately
ICP >22 mmHg sustained despite tier-one measures (ENLS v6.0; BTF 4th ed. ch. 16)
Rising Na/Cl or creatinine limiting further osmotherapy
institutionVaries: HTS concentrations stocked, bolus volumes (not specified by NCS 2020 or ENLS v6.0 ICP module), and peripheral administration policy
Na target strategy (bolus vs targeted infusion)
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the acute treatment of cerebral edema in neurocritical care patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32(3):647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7
